_doc: Meshes and lights for Kod-placed objects (data/zone_layout.json objects, by class), docs/adr/0003 pass 3. tools/ue/build_world.py spawns `mesh` (build/environment/kit/<mesh>.glb, tools/blender/build_prop_kit.py) at the object's position, plus a warm point light `offset_m` above it. Light intensity in candela; at ~8 lux of daylight these read as glows and become the main light in deep shade and at night. `candela_scale`: a factor on a Kod light's candela (2026-10-06: the braziers and lamps dimmed twice by 25%, to 0.56 of the original, at the user's request: too bright at night). `kod_intensity` / `kod_color` (a light): the Kod class's light (0-255, 15-bit colour), overridden by the object's own iIntensity / iColor; build_world.py turns them into candela (0.24 per unit), reach (4 m + 0.15 per unit) and colour (DynamicLight: the invisible lights the original places in rooms; Candle). `shadows`: false for unshadowed pools of light, as the original's. `night_only` (a light, or a material slot): off from 11 to 17 like the original lamps (kod lamp.kod), switched by the environment director in game (docs/adr/0005). `materials`: the kit's material slots (linear colours; emissive in nits-ish scene units); zone art uses them as 'prop_<name>' slots too (window boxes).

smoke._doc: Chimney smoke (docs/adr/0005 phase 5): tools/environment/chimneys.py finds every chimney the blockout draws with these wall textures, and build_world.py stands a plume (SM_Puffs with M_Smoke, materials.json "smoke") on each top. How much smoke: moods.json "atmosphere" "smoke". A class's "moths": moths circle its light at night, offset_m above the object (SM_Puffs with M_Moth).

fires._doc: Flame presets (docs/adr/0005 phase 3). Each is a flipbook of the original's own flame frames: "texture" (a wall texture's animation frames) or "bgf" + "frames" (an object's, from python tools/bgf2png/bgf2png.py <name>), cropped to "crop" [x0, y0, x1, y1] (original pixels; "keep": "flame" keeps only flame-coloured pixels, "all" every opaque one), upscaled by make_placeholders.py into T_Fire_<name> and drawn by AMRFireActor as a camera-facing sprite at the original's size, cycling at "fps" (each fire from its own phase) with emissive "brightness". "walls": wall textures with this flame painted on (the wall torches): "at" the flame centre in the texture's pixels, "out" the texture direction pointing away from the wall it's mounted on, "erase" the rect whose flame-coloured pixels are made transparent; tools/environment/fires.py finds every flame where the blockout uses them, and "light" lights each (the original torches had none of their own: their sectors were lit). A class's "fire": the preset, and "base_m" the height of the flame's bottom above the object. "flicker" on a light: true always, "sector" only in the original's flickering sectors (SF_FLICKER); flickering lights are spawned as AMRFireActor and driven by UMRFireSubsystem (seeded noise, about the original's +-40 of 255, a shadow budget for the nearest few).
